papers.title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived spheroids and microtissues for biofabrication: advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies.
papers.abstract: Biofabrication integrates biological and engineering principles to generate functional tissues for regenerative medicine, drug screening, and disease modeling. Among the diverse cellular sources available, mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as a critical component due to their multipotency, immunomodulatory capacity, and scalability. This review focuses on MSC-derived spheroids and microtissues as building blocks for biofabrication, organizing recent advances in bioassembly and bioprinting strategies around the axis of undifferentiated versus pre-differentiated microtissues and how the timing of differentiation shapes construct functionality. Key technological innovations, including dynamic culture systems, scaffold-free assembly, and high-resolution bioprinting (e.g. droplet-based), have enabled enhanced control over microtissue maturation and structural fidelity. The role of the cellular microenvironment in determining MSC fate is examined, emphasizing how biochemical cues, mechanical properties, and oxygen gradients can be engineered during microtissue formation. Cellular heterogeneity is addressed as a path-dependent variable continuously reshaped by donor-specific factors (age, sex, health status) and process-imposed cues (isolation methods, expansion conditions, and mechanical stress) throughout thein vitrolife cycle, and concrete mitigation strategies are discussed, including prospective cell sorting and a proposed functional potency panel (extracellular matrix deposition, fusion competence, and secretome profiling), alongside recent advancements in automated and machine learning-based biofabrication platforms. Vascularization and immunological integration are examined as central translation bottlenecks, covering endothelial co-culture, prevascularized spheroids, sacrificial bioprinting, and MSC-driven modulation of the host immune response. By integrating the fabrication route, heterogeneity as a manufacturing process variable, and translational/regulatory bottlenecks into a single framework, this review highlights recent advances, discusses current limitations, and outlines future directions for clinical translation of MSC-based biofabrication.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该综述聚焦MSC球体与生物打印策略，仅在末尾提及机器学习平台，未将AI嵌入生物打印工作流，与AI for Bioprinting方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This review does not integrate AI/ML into any specific bioprinting workflow stage; machine learning is only briefly mentioned as an emerging platform without experimental AI validation or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 系统梳理MSC来源球体与微组织作为生物制造构建单元的最新进展。
summary_zh.method: 以未分化与预分化微组织为轴线，综述动态培养、无支架组装、高分辨率生物打印及微环境调控策略。
summary_zh.result: 归纳了细胞异质性作为制造变量的缓解策略，并指出血管化与免疫整合是临床转化瓶颈。

summary_en.motivation: To consolidate recent progress in MSC-derived spheroids and microtissues as building blocks for biofabrication.
summary_en.method: The review organizes bioassembly and bioprinting strategies along the axis of undifferentiated versus pre-differentiated microtissues, covering dynamic culture, scaffold-free assembly, high-resolution printing, and microenvironmental control.
summary_en.result: It proposes heterogeneity mitigation strategies such as prospective cell sorting and a functional potency panel, and identifies vascularization and immunological integration as key translation bottlenecks.
summary_en.validation: Narrative literature review without experimental validation.
